solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Relax and maybe monitor gigolo

parts.note: to relax lazily
a monitor is one kind of large reptile, hence 'maybe'

explanation.surface: Someone told to relax and keep an eye on a kept man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Monitor' reads as a verb meaning watch, but here it is the noun: a monitor lizard, given with 'maybe' because it is just one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Both terms describe an idle man who seeks the company and money of wealthy women in bars and salons.

clue.text: Inclined to report fast time

indicators.note: a report is something spoken or heard, so the word wanted is one that merely sounds right

parts.note: Lent is the Christian season of fasting before Easter

explanation.surface: A reporter keen on writing about a quick race time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast time' looks like a quick lap, but it is a period of fasting: LENT. In British speech LEANT is pronounced the same way.
explanation.definitionFit: Past tense of lean: something that tilted or sloped was inclined, matching the participle form exactly.

clue.text: Open in advance

definitions.meaning: first meaning: candid, frank and honest
second meaning: beforehand, as with a payment

explanation.walkthrough: The three words read as one phrase about opening early; split them into two separate meanings of the same expression.
explanation.definitionFit: Being upfront means being candid about things, and paying upfront means settling a bill beforehand.

clue.text: Did Gauguin ever envision hiding a legendary queen?

indicators.note: whatever hides something keeps it concealed within itself, so the letters lie inside the phrase

parts.note: runs across the painter's surname and the next two words

explanation.surface: Asking whether the French painter ever pictured a mythical royal in his work.
explanation.walkthrough: The painter's name is a natural camouflage: the end of Gauguin, all of 'ever' and the start of 'envision' spell her name.
explanation.definitionFit: King Arthur's wife in the Camelot stories, a queen from medieval British romance and myth.

clue.text: See 1
At first, ICE terrorises and loots your country

indicators.note: taking each word at its first point means keeping only its opening letter

parts.note: initials of the five words

explanation.surface: A news line about US immigration enforcement raiding and plundering a reader's homeland.
explanation.walkthrough: ICE is the US Immigration and Customs Enforcement agency, which makes the surface topical; its capital I is simply the first initial.
explanation.definitionFit: The southern European nation with Rome as its capital is a country.

clue.text: Not repeating cataclysmic disaster when mast was lost

indicators.note: a disaster leaves things in chaos, so the remaining letters are thrown into a new order
what is lost goes missing, so some letters disappear from the word

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written; these four letters are removed

explanation.surface: A shipwreck so catastrophic that, with the mast gone, it will never happen again.
explanation.walkthrough: Strike M, A, S and T from CATACLYSMIC to leave CACLYIC, then rearrange those seven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something without cycles has no recurring pattern, so it is non-periodic and never comes round again.

clue.text: Bold laugh misplaced round bread

indicators.note: letters put in the wrong place end up in a different arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone guffawing loudly at the wrong moment around a loaf.
explanation.walkthrough: The nine letters of the two opening words rearrange exactly into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A small baked or boiled ball of dough, often served with pizza or stew, is bread in spherical form.

clue.text: Can just be part of London

parts.note: 'you may' means you are permitted, you can
just and fair both mean equitable

explanation.surface: A wry remark that a mere tin could be a piece of the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can' looks like a noun and 'just' like 'merely'; they are the verb and the adjective. Mayfair is an expensive district of central London.
explanation.definitionFit: The wealthy West End neighbourhood near Hyde Park is one district of the British capital.

clue.text: Bald guy confused with insect

indicators.note: confused things are muddled up, so the letters lose their order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A hairless man mistaken for a bug.
explanation.walkthrough: The seven letters of the first two words rearrange into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The red, black-spotted beetle (ladybird in Britain) is a small flying insect.

clue.text: Group reduced charge for delivery

parts.note: ELO, the Electric Light Orchestra, a British rock band
cut prices are reduced ones
an ion is a charged particle

explanation.surface: A firm offering a discounted fee for delivering parcels.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about postage; 'delivery' is actually the manner of speaking, and 'charge' is electrical.
explanation.definitionFit: Elocution is the art of clear speaking, and a speaker's delivery is their style of voicing words.

clue.text: Links format of deed with latitude

parts.note: a stroke is an act or feat, as in a stroke of genius
play is freedom of movement, room to manoeuvre

explanation.surface: Website links that give the layout of a legal document with geographic coordinates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Links' suggests web links or a chain, but a links is a seaside golf course; 'deed' and 'latitude' are not legal or geographic here.
explanation.definitionFit: Stroke play is the golf scoring method that counts total shots taken, a competition format played on any course.

clue.text: Chinese people haul wreckage

indicators.note: wreckage is something smashed apart, so the letters are broken up and reassembled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: People in China dragging away debris from a crash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wreckage' looks like the object being hauled, but it signals the rearrangement of the word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lahu are an ethnic minority group living in Yunnan in south-west China and neighbouring countries.

clue.text: Beat by a distance

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the rhythmic pattern of verse or music
second meaning: the basic metric unit of length

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like winning a race comfortably; 'Beat' is a noun, rhythm, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: In poetry the measured rhythm is called metre, and the same word names a unit of length of 100 centimetres.

clue.text: Remark has upset city

indicators.note: something upset is knocked over and disordered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A tactless comment that has offended a whole town.
explanation.walkthrough: The nine letters of the first two words rearrange into the city's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Marrakesh is a major historic city in Morocco, famous for its medina and souks.

clue.text: Human tests contracted officers swallowing tea

indicators.note: to swallow something is to take it inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: the short form of captains
cha (or char) is British slang for tea

explanation.surface: Officers in a trial drinking tea while running experiments on people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contracted' sounds like hired, but it means abbreviated: Capts.
explanation.definitionFit: Those website puzzles of distorted letters exist to check that a visitor is a person rather than a bot.

clue.text: Sleuth holds record for working with Italian banger

indicators.note: to hold something is to keep it inside, so one piece is placed within another

parts.note: PI, private investigator
an EP is an extended-play record
per means for, as in 'per person'
a machine that is working is on

explanation.surface: A detective keeping a file on an Italian who is working with an explosive device.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banger' suggests a firework or explosive, fitting the detective story, but a banger is British slang for a sausage.
explanation.definitionFit: Pepperoni is a spicy cured salami of Italian-American origin, so it is a kind of sausage.

clue.text: Clergyman holds Channel Islands most dear

indicators.note: something that holds another keeps it inside its own walls

parts.note: a priest is a clergyman
CI is the abbreviation for the Channel Islands

explanation.surface: A vicar who loves the islands off Normandy more than anywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most dear' suggests most beloved, but it means most expensive. The Channel Islands are British Crown dependencies near France, such as Jersey and Guernsey.
explanation.definitionFit: Dear in the sense of costly, so the superlative is the most expensive, the highest priced.

clue.text: Bucking bronco is first injected with energy

indicators.note: an injection puts something inside, so one piece is placed within another
a horse that bucks throws itself about, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter only

parts.note: the initial of the word

explanation.surface: A wild horse given a shot of something to pep it up.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange BRONCO as CONBRO, then slip I between the R and the final O.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian musical direction telling the performer to play vigorously, with spirit and vigour.

clue.text: Opening for light dog investigating leather leads

parts.note: a pup is a young dog

indicators.note: leaders go at the front, so only each word's opening letter is kept

parts.note: initials of the two words

explanation.surface: A sniffer dog checking out leather dog leads, with an opening note on lighting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leads' looks like dog leashes, fitting the surface, but it means the leading letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The black aperture in the centre of the iris admits rays into the eye, a hole that lets light through.

clue.text: Swineherds take time in the shade

parts.note: men who look after pigs
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Pig farmers taking a break out of the sun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shade' suggests shelter from the sun, but it is a colour; 'take time' means add a T.
explanation.definitionFit: A pigment is a substance giving colour, and a shade is a particular colour or tint.

clue.text: Fall for Spain's plain features

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to come down from the sky as water

definitions.note: an allusion to a song line rather than a synonym
definitions.meaning: second meaning: what the elocution song in My Fair Lady says stays mainly in the plain

explanation.walkthrough: The line 'The rain in Spain stays mainly in the plain' is Eliza Doolittle's elocution exercise in My Fair Lady.
explanation.definitionFit: Rain falls from clouds as precipitation, and the famous song places Spanish showers chiefly on the lowlands.

clue.text: Rose perhaps to be attendant to the bride

definitions.note: a whimsical reading: Rose is both a flower and a girl's name
definitions.meaning: first meaning: a girl named after a bloom, one example of many such names
second meaning: a young girl who scatters petals at a wedding

explanation.surface: A girl called Rose who might be asked to attend the bride at a wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: Rose is a woman's name that is also a bloom, so a girl called Rose is a girl with a flower's name.
explanation.definitionFit: At a wedding a small girl carries a basket of petals ahead of the bride as one of her attendants.

clue.text: Fire Spanish leaders for frustrating USA's excessively gung-ho operation

definitions.note: the Spanish word for fire, not an English synonym

indicators.note: leaders go at the front, so only the opening letter of each word counts

parts.note: initials of the four words

explanation.surface: Sacking Spain's leaders for thwarting an overzealous American military mission.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fire' sounds like dismissing someone, but it is the noun, wanted in Spanish. The first letters run F, U, E, G, O, starting with 'for'.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Spanish language the word for flames or a blaze is this one, as in the Tierra del Fuego islands.

clue.text: It's official — extremely risible First Lady

indicators.note: at the extremes means at the two ends, so only the outermost letters stay

parts.note: first and last letters of the word
Eve was the first woman in the Bible

explanation.surface: A declaration that the President's wife is officially ridiculous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First Lady' suggests a president's spouse, but it is Eve, the first woman in Genesis.
explanation.definitionFit: A reeve was a local magistrate or administrator in medieval England, the origin of the word sheriff (shire reeve).

clue.text: Student is second class breadwinner

indicators.note: the second of a word is the letter in position two

parts.note: the letter in position two
a breadwinner earns the household income

explanation.surface: A student who is a second-class earner in the household.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second class' reads as a lowly rank, but it means the second letter of 'class'.
explanation.definitionFit: A student is a person acquiring knowledge or skills, so both terms name someone being taught.

clue.text: Let down by third guess in Wordle disaster

indicators.note: a piece that is in another sits within it
a disaster leaves everything in chaos, so the letters end up scrambled

parts.note: taken as written; the online word game

indicators.note: the third of a word is the letter in position three

parts.note: the letter in position three

explanation.surface: Feeling disappointed by a disastrous third attempt at the daily word puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Let down' reads as disappointed, which suits the surface, but it means physically brought lower.
explanation.definitionFit: To let something down is to lower it, as with a rope or a drawbridge, so the past forms match.

clue.text: Magic cape at Oscars

parts.note: a hood is a cape-like covering, as on an academic gown
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet, so two of them

explanation.surface: A magician's cloak on show at the Academy Awards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oscars' suggests the film awards but stands for the letter O twice, from radio spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoodoo is African-American folk sorcery, so it is a kind of witchcraft or spell-working.

clue.text: Tell it's wrong toy

indicators.note: something wrong is out of order, so the letters are rearranged correctly

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone telling a child their plaything is broken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Toy' looks like a plaything noun, but it is the adjective used of small dog breeds, as in toy poodle.
explanation.definitionFit: A toy breed is a miniature version, so toy works as an adjective meaning small or tiny.
